#3120. ESR Black Friday gift guide: Premium accessories for iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, iPad, AirPods, and Apple Watch

If you picked up a new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo this fall, or you’re shopping for someone with an iPad, AirPods, or Apple Watch, there’s a good chance you’ve been holding out on purchasing accessories until all of the Black Friday deals started. We’ve got you covered with some great deals on premium accessories for nearly every Apple device on your list.

ESR has been making Apple accessories since 2009, and that track record has made it a trustworthy name for the more than 123 million people who use its products to protect their Apple devices and make them more versatile. Here’s a look at what’s included in ESR’s Black Friday lineup and who each one is for.

If someone on your shopping list picked up an iPhone Duo, a case is the first thing they need, and it’s also the hardest one to get right. As we’ve seen with Android foldables, you’re protecting two halves, a hinge, and a phone that changes shape throughout the day as you use it, all without adding bulk to a device people bought because it folds thin. ESR has two options for iPhone Duo owners, and the choice mostly comes down to the look you want to achieve.

The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand is your choice if you want to show off your iPhone Duo’s colors. It combines a rigid polycarbonate and acrylic back with a softer TPU frame. The rigid back keeps the case from flexing and lets the iPhone Duo’s design show through, while the flexible frame absorbs the shock if you drop it (please don’t).

The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand is perfect for those who want a more premium look for their iPhone Duo. It’s made from organic silicone leather with a soft, skin-friendly feel and a stain-resistant finish. If you’ve ever used a light-colored leather case before, you know it usually shows every stain and smudge it comes across, but ESR built the Atelier to resist daily wear and wipe clean.

Both cases share ESR’s Flex Stand, and it’s one of the most innovative and versatile parts of the lineup. It’s a 180-degree rotating stand made from zinc alloy, so it holds its shape even after months of propping up your iPhone. A precision hinge with damping control lets it open smoothly and lock at the angle you choose, whether the iPhone Duo is folded or unfolded, and ESR says it has passed 3,000 open-and-close tests. In real life, that means propping the iPhone Duo open on a desk for a video call or on an airplane tray table for a movie, then using the stand as a grip when you’re holding it.

Both cases add extra hinge protection and raised edges where a foldable is most exposed. If you follow our MagSafe Monday column, you know magnetic strength really matters for MagSafe wallets, car mounts, etc. The Classic Hybrid has 1,500g of magnetic hold, and the Atelier has 1,400g.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case for iPhone Duo is 15% off.

The same two incredible cases come in iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max versions, and they also fit the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand has a clear back, a TPU frame, and a PU anti-yellowing coating. In simple terms, TPU is the flexible, shock-absorbing plastic used in most case frames, and it’s also what usually turns clear cases slightly yellow the longer you use them, so ESR adds a polyurethane (PU) coating to shield it. ESR upgraded the case’s UV protection for longer-lasting resistance to yellowing, and it’s SGS-certified for anti-yellowing. A clear case is supposed to show off your iPhone’s color, so staying clear longer is the whole point. The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand retains the same soft silicone leather and stain-resistant finish as the iPhone Duo version.

On these models, the Flex Stand adjusts from 15 to 69 degrees for portrait and landscape viewing. That has you covered for StandBy mode on your nightstand and a show over your lunch break, with no separate stand to carry around.

Protection is where the two cases differ. ESR rates the Classic Hybrid for 4x military-grade protection with 16-foot drop protection, plus a full-coverage camera bar. The Atelier is rated for 3x military-grade protection, including 12-foot drop protection, and features a soft microfiber lining. Military-grade refers to the MIL-STD-810 drop test, which uses a 4-foot drop, so 4x and 3x mean ESR rates the cases for four and three times that height. Both include a built-in Camera Control cover and raised edges, and both use a precise magnetic ring layout that automatically aligns with MagSafe chargers, car mounts, wallets, and batteries.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case is up to 28% off, and the ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case is up to 37% off.

A case protects everything except the part you touch all day. The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector covers the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and the name is worth unpacking. Armorite is ESR’s line of toughened screen protectors, and the Pro version is made with Accessory Glass by Corning™. Corning has made the durable glass in Apple products since the very first iPhone, so in non-tech speak, this is glass from a trustworthy name rather than generic tempered glass.

Why it matters: ESR says the protector delivers 10x the impact absorption of generic protectors, and Corning’s lab testing shows up to 2x better scratch performance and up to 25% less scratch visibility for its Accessory Glass. When you drop your iPhone or toss it in a pocket with your keys, the protector takes the hit instead of your screen. An anti-reflective coating reduces light reflection to just 2.3% while maintaining 94% optical transmittance, resulting in less glare outside and truer color. Edge-to-edge coverage leaves no gaps for dust to collect.

Installation is the part most people dread on a brand-new iPhone, and ESR’s UltraFit tray handles it in two steps. Pull the tab, and the tray’s design clears dust and pushes out air bubbles as the glass goes down. Long gone are the days when you needed “professional installation” for a screen protector to look great.

Black Friday deal: The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector is 15% off.

Holiday travel usually means one open outlet, an iPhone, a laptop, an e-reader, etc., that all need power, and cables left at home. The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger builds the cable in. It has a braided cable that extends to 3.1 feet and fully retracts into the charger, and ESR rates it for 20,000 pulls and 10,000 bends. An extra USB-C port lets a second device charge simultaneously. 9to5Mac’s Michael Burkhardt went hands-on with the Xtend 45W earlier this month and said it’s an excellent iPhone fast charger on the go.

It’s rated at 45 watts and delivers up to 60 watts of dynamic power, enough to fast-charge phones and laptops, and it works with iPhone Duo, iPhone 15 through 18, and Android phones like Galaxy and Pixel. It supports PD 3.2 AVS, which in plain English means the charger and your device talk to each other, and the charger fine-tunes the power it sends to exactly what that device asks for. ESR says it can charge an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max to 50% in about 15 minutes. It’s also TÜV-certified, meaning an independent testing organization has verified its safety features.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger is up to 32% off from November 20 through December 1.

For the student or anyone who does real work on an iPad, the ESR Shift Keyboard Case makes for an incredible gift. The Bluetooth keyboard attaches magnetically and comes off when you don’t need it, so you can type an essay at a desk, then pull the keyboard away to watch something on the couch or sketch with the iPad flat on a table.

ESR built the Shift around five modes designed to make your iPad even more versatile. Productivity mode lets you detach the keyboard and type over Bluetooth, so the iPad can sit on a desk while the keyboard sits on your lap. Landscape mode adjusts from 20 to 75 degrees for typing and watching, Portrait mode holds 70 degrees for reading, browsing in Safari, or making a FaceTime call, and Drawing mode drops to a stable 20 degrees for sketching and editing with your Apple Pencil. Hands-On mode lets you hold the iPad like a regular tablet. An iPad is a laptop one minute and a tablet the next, and the Shift is designed to keep up with all of your iPad use cases.

For a student, that means taking notes in class with the keyboard attached, then detaching it to annotate a PDF or review flashcards on the couch. For someone who travels for work, it means answering email on a tray table, then pulling the keyboard off to watch a movie on the flight home. One case covers both, and the keyboard pairs and reconnects easily when you snap it back on.

The trackpad is fully clickable and supports all the multi-touch gestures you already use on your iPad. Apple Pencil gets a home too. ESR’s Dual Smart Pencil Storage uses a magnetic holder and an elastic sleeve, so your Pencil stays with your iPad instead of rolling around the bottom of your bag. Its Air Guard corners protect your iPad when it’s stowed away.

The ESR Shift Keyboard Case comes in versions for iPad Pro 11-inch and 13-inch (M4 and M5), iPad Air 11-inch and 13-inch (including the new M4 models), and iPad (A16), so whichever iPad you’re trying to take to the next level of productivity, there’s a Shift that fits it.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Shift Keyboard Case is up to 25% off, depending on your iPad model.

Have you ever dropped your AirPods case and watched the earbuds go flying? With the Cyber FlickLock, you won’t have to worry about that. We’ve covered FlickLock in MagSafe Monday before, but let’s recap it.

When the internal latch is engaged, the magnets line up to attract each other and hold the lid shut with maximum force, adding a second layer of security. Slide the button, and the magnets shift to repel each other, so the lid pops open with one hand. ESR says the slide mechanism has been tested over 20,000 times.

The result is that your AirPods stay in the case if you drop it. Both cases also have 260g of magnetic strength, so they snap onto MagSafe chargers, Apple Watch chargers, and MagSafe batteries if you need to charge your AirPods. Again, it’s extremely strong, but extremely easy to unlock with one hand.

The ESR Cyber FlickLock Magnetic Case is extremely durable and has a clip hook, so you can hang your AirPods on a backpack while hiking or cycling. The ESR Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Case brings the same lock in a range of vibrant colors with a carrying lanyard, so you can wear your AirPods on your wrist or attach them to a bag. Both cases come in versions for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 and 1, and AirPods 5 and 4. No matter which AirPods you or your loved one have, this is the case everyone will love.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Cyber FlickLock and Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Cases are both 20% off.

The ESR Equinox Watch Band is a quick pick for anyone who works out in the morning while tracking progress with Apple Watch, then heads to the office. A pin-and-fold lock keeps it secure, and it’s made from HNBR, a durable, skin-friendly synthetic rubber that resists water and tearing, with ventilation cutouts for all-day comfort. It fits 44mm, 45mm, 46mm, and 49mm models across Apple Watch Ultra 1 through 4, Series 4 through 12, and SE 1 through 3, and it comes in several colors to match your outfit or your mood that day.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Equinox Watch Band is 20% off.

The best gifts are the ones that get used every day, and accessories are the part of the Apple experience people live with the most. A case that props up a foldable, a screen protector made with Corning glass, a charger with a built-in cable, and an AirPods case that stays closed even when dropped check all the boxes. ESR truly makes something for everyone and is one of the most trusted names in the Apple accessories ecosystem.

ESR built its Black Friday lineup around the whole Apple ecosystem, from the new iPhone Duo to iPad, AirPods, and even a great Apple Watch band, with premium materials and versatile designs that are durable, functional, and great-looking. ESR’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals run on Amazon from November 19 through November 30 (the Xtend 45W runs through December 1), with discounts of up to 37%!

#3117. Bausch Health: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Mandatory Medicare price cuts on a flagship drug will test whether the company's cash generation can fund growth investments without derailing long-term value creation.

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 23, 2026 at 3:00PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Bausch Health Companies ›

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Bausch Health (BHC +1.34%) raised its full-year 2026 guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, which measures core operating profit before non-cash charges, and operating cash flow. Steady cash generation gives the business the balance sheet flexibility to pay down debt and invest in new drug candidates.

Bausch Health reduced its net debt, or total debt minus cash, by more than $500 million during the quarter. That cash creation lets management pay down obligations while repurchasing outstanding public debt.

Salix, the company's gastrointestinal drug segment, faces mandatory price reductions on Xifaxan, its flagship gut treatment, under government Medicare regulations. Management must adjust its gross to net accrual, an accounting estimate for revenue deductions, to account for those lower price caps.

Beyond current drugs, Bausch Health relies on larsucosterol, an experimental liver disease compound, to drive future revenue. The drug is in Phase 3, the final stage of clinical testing before regulatory submission, targeting alcohol-associated hepatitis.

Revenue growth is accelerating across international markets, and leadership isn't hiding its satisfaction with operational discipline. Global commercial scale, diversified pharmaceutical offerings, and expanding profit margins provide long-term resilience as management monitors commercial execution.

Long-term expansion depends on managing debt obligations while reallocating cash toward targeted research programs.

#3116. Apple @ Work: Workbrew 2.0 is an inventory for the development software your employees installed without asking

Apple @ Work is exclusively brought to you by Mosyle, the only Apple Unified Platform. Mosyle is the only solution that integrates in a single professional grade platform all the solutions necessary to seamlessly and automatically deploy, manage, and protect Apple devices at work. Over 45,000 organizations trust Mosyle to make millions of Apple devices work ready with no effort and at an affordable cost. Request your EXTENDED TRIAL today and understand why Mosyle is everything you need to work with Apple.

If you ask any Mac admin for a list of the software on their fleet, they’ll pull up their device management inventory and show you the apps they’ve deployed. Ask them what their developers installed with Homebrew last month, which VS Code extensions they are running, or what npm pulled into a project on Tuesday, and you’ll get a different response. That software was never procured by finance, never approved, and never inventoried. It’s also where a growing share of the risk lives in the AI era. Workbrew 2.0 treats that gap as a problem worth solving for IT teams.

About Apple @ Work: Bradley Chambers has been an Apple IT admin since 2009. Through his experience deploying and managing firewalls, switches, a mobile device management system, enterprise grade WiFi, 1000s of Macs, and 1000s of iPads, Bradley will highlight ways in which Apple IT managers deploy Apple devices, build networks to support them, train users, share stories from the trenches of IT management, and ways Apple could improve its products for IT departments.

Device management is built around the software IT deploys. Apps from Apple Business Manager, apps preloaded via your device management vendors’ packages, packages you upload, and profiles you push out. That model solves the problem for native macOS apps. It doesn’t cover what happens when the Mac becomes the default developer machine. Developers install what they need with a single command in Terminal, and Homebrew alone has more than 16,000 packages. You then add millions of npm packages and hundreds of thousands of IDE extensions, and the list of software on a Mac that IT didn’t put there is longer than the list it did.

That used to be a developer-only problem. It isn’t anymore, in the vibe-coding era. AI tools have turned marketers, analysts, and ops people into builders, and those builders install packages too.

Workbrew started as a management layer for Homebrew: an agent that reports what’s installed, flags known vulnerabilities, and lets IT push updates across the fleet. Version 2.0 expands the catalog to include npm packages, VS Code extensions, and macOS apps, all in a single inventory. The company says it has patched more than 10 million vulnerabilities for customers since its launch, and it’s now ISO 27001-certified.

The part that is critical for everyone who isn’t a developer is the new Workbrew app, a native Mac app for finding, installing, and updating approved software. Workbrew calls it “the app store for your entire company.” Employees can browse what IT has approved, install it without opening Terminal, and request anything that isn’t on the list. IT approves or denies in the Workbrew Console, and if it’s a no, the employee gets an answer on why.

The app comes from the Updatest team, which Workbrew acquired as part of this release. Updatest is the indie Mac app that keeps thousands of users’ software up to date, and it remains a separate product for individuals and families. For business customer, that experience is now the Workbrew app, and it’s included on every plan, including the free Team plan with no device or user limits.

With Workbrew, we finally have real visibility into what developers are using in Homebrew. Fleet-wide updates are effortless, and the team stays secure without being slowed down.

Chris Merrell, Director of IT, End User Services, Camping World

Workbrew isn’t a device management tool and isn’t trying to be one. Your device management system deploys the Workbrew agent, and Workbrew handles software your device management system lacks visibility into. If your fleet consists entirely of office workers on managed apps, there’s nothing here for you. If you have developers, or you’ve noticed the marketing team installing things to run AI scripts, you have the problem whether you’ve discovered it or not.

AI tools have changed how we think about app management, because apps get installed differently now. Workbrew 2.0 provides IT with a list of development tools on the Mac and gives employees a sanctioned way to get what they need.

Workbrew 2.0 is now available with a free Team plan and no device or user limits.

At its lowest ever price, the Pixel 11 Pro is finally worth buying

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I say this every year, and I always get proven right. Buying a Google Pixel phone at launch is a waste of money, and the Pixel 11 Pro has proven to be no exception; after just three months on sale, the latest Pixel flagship has lost almost a third off its original price — hitting its lowest price so far.

You can pick up the Pixel 11 Pro for $749 in Amazon's Black Friday sale. That's $350 off the usual price, and it all but wipes out the last few years of price hikes Google has been subjecting us to. The regular Pro isn't the only one getting that discount either, since the Pixel 11 Pro XL is $899 in Amazon's Black Friday sale. That's $400 off, and another all-time low for the largest Google phone of 2026.

The Google Pixel 11 Pro was a little disappointing when it launched, especially if you were paying full price. But with $350 off? The apparent lack of meaningful upgrades isn't so bad. Especially since you do still get a brighter screen, HiLight, new AI features and better cameras.

If you'd rather have a bigger screen and battery, the Pixel 11 Pro XL can be yours for $150 more. The benefits are basically the same, but if you need that extra real estate and longevity, this is probably the Pixel to get.

One of my biggest gripes with the Google Pixel 11 Pro (and Pro XL) is that the upgrades you get over the Pixel 10 Pro are pretty minimal. So I resented that not only did Google charge full price for such a mediocre upgrade, but it also increased the price by $100. But with $350 off? That's basically the same price Pixel phones were three or four years ago, when they were considered a cheaper option — which is always a good thing.

So what are you actually getting for your money? The best thing about the standard Pixel 11 Pro is that it now comes with 256GB of storage as standard, which means you get double the space compared to the cheapest Pixel 10 Pro. On top of that, Google has improved the display on both sizes and turned up the screen brightness once again.

The best part of any new Google phone is the improvements to the cameras and AI performance. The ultrawide and telephoto lenses in particular benefit from larger sensors, improving the overall camera quality, and the AI enhancements mean that the new 120x zoom actually feels like magic.

Other AI-powered additions include the new Magic Capture mode, which records video and pulls out the best stills as static photos. The new Rambler dictation mode is also significantly better than Google's old voice-to-text system, thanks to its ability to understand commands in a conversational way. I did experience some issues with this when I tested Rambler, so it is far from perfect.

Google also added a Live Translation feature which automatically converts any foreign language you hear on YouTube into your chosen tongue — in my case, English. There's also the customizable HiLight notification alert on the back, for those of you who tend to keep your devices face down.

Usual Pixel pitfalls still apply, though. Battery life could be better, and performance is appalling compared to rivals like Apple and Google. The base level of RAM has been reduced from 16GB to 12GB too, which means you'll need to buy the 1TB storage option to maximize the available memory.

Still, with prices dropping as far as this, grabbing the Pixel 11 Pro for $799 is well worth considering. It's not often a flagship device ends up this cheap, even if it isn't quite as powerful as rival flagships.

#3114. How Microcredentials Can Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

IEEE Credentialing Program pairs AI governance standards with microcredentials

Kaitlyn Ridel is the IEEE microcredentials marketing specialist.

Engineering teams are moving at breakneck speed to integrate artificial intelligence, but they are running into a formidable new barrier: compliance issues. Translating high-level AI ethics, governance, and auditing into daily operational workflows has become one of the industry’s toughest challenges.

“AI ethics” refers to the principles developers use to govern and operate workflows. “Governance” refers to the rules and procedures an organization establishes for AI workflows and how they interact with organizational data. Auditing is the process of assessing and validating systems to ensure safety, fairness, transparency, and legal compliance.

Technology leads and systems engineers are responsible for adhering to a structured set of guidelines for standards and processes usually issued by a governing body such as the European Union, the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, and the International Organization for Standardization.

The regulations aim to mitigate issues such as systemic bias, security vulnerabilities, and transparency risks, but they also highlight a critical skills gap.

Most traditional computer science, software, and electrical engineering degree programs were built around technical design and system architecture. They do not yet include training in AI auditing, data tracking, or safety protocols for how AI systems interact with people and other technologies.

Expecting mid-career engineers to leave their job to attend a full-time two- or four-year program to learn about the topics is not feasible. Yet treating safety and governance as an afterthought can lead to costly product delays, legal exposure, and broken public trust.

Targeted microcredential programs can bridge the knowledge gap by helping engineers build skills in compliance, AI ethics, and governance.

Skills-based microcredentials represent the mastery of expertise gained through a learning program. To earn them, learners must demonstrate the skill through a validation assessment. The microcredentials can be stacked, showing a growing skill set in a defined area and allowing learners to earn several microcredentials in one program.

Microcredentials also allow engineers to upskill and master critical competencies, such as bias mitigation, algorithmic transparency, and risk auditing, without interrupting their career. Through rigorous skills-validation assessments, microcredentials give tech leaders verifiable proof that their teams can audit systems effectively before deployment.

For engineering organizations, microcredentialing creates an agile upskilling pathway. It connects software engineering and hardware design directly to regulatory frameworks, empowering teams to certify systems for safety and compliance within their development life cycles.

Bridging technical capability and ethical responsibility requires a trusted foundation. IEEE has long been a pioneer in socio-technical standards, most notably through the IEEE 7000 series for ethics in AI system design, a framework created to address ethical considerations during the development life cycle.

The IEEE Credentialing Program translates the organization’s world-class standards into actionable, industry-aligned microcredentials. For more than three decades, IEEE has set the gold standard for technical validation and professional certification. By pairing cutting-edge AI governance standards with targeted microcredential programs, IEEE provides engineers and IT leaders with clear, standardized road maps to build systems that are not just technically advanced but also safe, compliant, and worthy of public trust.

To learn more about the credentialing program, explore the offerings or connect with an IEEE expert.

Kaitlyn Ridel is a marketing specialist for the IEEE Microcredentialing Program

#3113. In 2026, 30% of All Money Invested in Stock ETFs Has Gone Into These 6 Popular Funds. Should These ETFs Be in Your Portfolio?

A surprisingly large percentage of new investor money is flowing into just a few index funds. Which ETF should you buy?

10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›

The stock market is going through a big sell-off right now, and the declines have come faster and more furiously than many people might have expected. In the past month (as of Nov. 20), the S&P 500 index (^GSPC +4.73%) is down more than 10%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 index has dropped by about 16%.

Big stock market sell-offs can cause many investors to question their choices and reevaluate their plans. If you've been trying to pick winning stocks, especially in the artificial intelligence (AI) space, some of your favorite names might be down 30%, 40%, 50%, or more. This can cause people to doubt themselves.

It's easy to feel like picking stocks is a good strategy when the stock market is going up, but when times get tough, that's when some investors decide they'd rather "buy the market" than try to "beat the market."

If the past month's stock market correction has made you want to stop picking stocks or boost the percentage of your portfolio that's invested in low-cost index funds, recent news from Bloomberg Intelligence suggests that you're not alone. A surprisingly large percentage of new investor money flowing into exchange-traded funds (ETFs) is going to just six index funds.

Let's look at which funds are attracting this big chunk of investor cash, and see which ETFs could be the right fit for your investment strategy.

According to Bloomberg reporting, as of Nov. 13, about 30% of all equity ETF flows in 2026 have gone to these six ETFs:

Bloomberg Intelligence also noted that the percentage of total equity ETF flows that have gone to these six funds has been increasing significantly since 2023. These six ETFs are all well-known index funds that track major benchmarks like the Nasdaq-100 or the S&P 500. The fact that these ETFs are becoming more popular is a sign that more investors are deciding to avoid the stock-picking game and just let the market do the hard work for them.

Let's look at a quick breakdown of each of these types of index funds, and see which could be the right fit for your future investments.

Four of these six popular ETFs identified by Bloomberg are funds that track the S&P 500 index. For many investors, one fund that holds those 500 large publicly traded companies might be the only ETF you need. S&P 500 ETFs offer broad diversification and a long-term track record of solid returns -- in the past 98 years, the S&P 500 index has delivered annualized returns of 9.98%.

The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF is the largest fund of its kind by assets under management. In the past five years, it's delivered annualized returns of about 12%.

Who should invest in these funds: Anyone who wants an easy, low-cost way to own the 500 most important companies in the U.S. stock market.

What if you want even more diversification than the 500 large-caps of the S&P 500? That's where a total stock market ETF can fit the bill. The Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) offers a portfolio of 3,511 U.S. stocks, and it includes small-caps and mid-caps, not just the major names of the S&P 500.

VTI generally tracks closely to the performance of the S&P 500, because those 500 large companies are so big, valuable, and influential on the overall market. But if small-caps and mid-caps start to outperform the larger companies, a fund like VTI might beat the S&P 500 in the future.

The Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF has delivered 10.95% annualized returns for the past five years (as of Oct. 31).

Who should invest in this fund: Long-term investors who want diversification and lower volatility than choosing individual stocks or sector ETFs.

What if you're not ready to give up on tech stocks, despite the recent tech sell-off? It's possible that investors' doubts about AI stocks are a temporary overreaction, and leading tech names will bounce back fast.

If you're bullish on tech stocks and you want to take a concentrated position in that sector, the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ +7.00%) can help you do that. This tech ETF holds 100 of the largest non-financial companies on the Nasdaq exchange. As of Oct. 31, QQQ had delivered annualized returns of about 13% for the past five years, and 20.3% for the past 10 years.

Who should invest in this fund: Investors who believe in the long-term prospects of the tech sector to outperform the rest of the market, and who are willing to accept the risks of higher volatility than they might get from an S&P 500 ETF or total stock market ETF.

#3111. 28 Zero-Day Findings in Under Two Days. Is Robotics Security Keeping Pace?

VicOne’s AI-assisted research reveals what faster zero-day discovery means for robot safety

VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety.

VicOne used AI to find 28 zero-day vulnerabilities in Physical AI tools —these weaknesses can impact robot training, testing, and real-world control.

This article is brought to you by VicOne.

VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem. These include projects developed or maintained by Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, among others.

Based on initial validation, all 28 findings are classified as zero-day vulnerabilities. The count may change following vendor and vulnerability-authority review, and some findings do not yet have CVE tracking numbers.

Many of these tools help teams train, simulate, test, and operate robots. Weaknesses in them could influence the models teams build, the test results they trust, and the instructions sent to robots.

These findings create two demands for robotics teams: responding as AI helps uncover weaknesses faster, and assessing how each one could affect robot safety and operations.

Vulnerability discovery involves examining code, tracing how systems communicate, and testing whether a suspected weakness can actually be exploited. AI can accelerate parts of this work, helping researchers analyze more software in less time. Attackers could use similar capabilities.

When the weakness is a zero-day — previously unknown and without an available fix — faster discovery can leave teams with little time to respond. While that exposure does not necessarily mean an attack has occurred, teams still need to determine whether they use the affected software and what an attacker could access or change.

VicOne’s findings span three stages of the robotics lifecycle: development and training, simulation and validation, and deployment and runtime. Weaknesses at each stage could affect what a robot learns, how it is tested, and how it is controlled.

Figure 1. In this research set, 75% of findings involved development, training, simulation, or validation tools, highlighting risks that can arise before a robot is deployed.VicOne

The following scenarios show how a compromised component could influence the robot at each stage.

These are potential consequences and not demonstrated outcomes for every finding. Actual effects depend on the attacker’s access, the system’s design, and whether other safeguards prevent the changes from reaching physical behavior.

In a separate demonstration, VicOne researchers provide a concrete example of a weakness affecting a protective function. The researchers exploited a vulnerability to prevent a robot’s remote-stop command from working. The case shows why teams need to test whether safeguards remain effective when the software supporting them is compromised.

Video 1. VicOne researchers demonstrate a vulnerability that prevents a robot’s remote-stop command from working. VicOne

AI can shorten the search for weaknesses, but a robotics team still needs to determine whether a fix is safe to deploy. Even after a software maintainer releases a patch, teams must identify affected systems, check compatibility, and verify that the update preserves intended behavior.

An earlier successful test remains useful evidence. However, a newly discovered weakness may reveal conditions that test never examined.

When immediate updating is impractical, teams may need temporary safeguards, such as restricting access to an affected service, while a validated fix is prepared.

As details from the 28 findings become available through coordinated disclosure, the next step is for robotics manufacturers is to connect each finding to its potential effect on development, deployment, and robot behavior.

That work also requires understanding how threats could affect robot behavior and how to protect systems already in operation. VicOne Radeis helps teams identify potential zero-day vulnerabilities, assess AI model and system security, and use simulation to evaluate how these risks could affect robot behavior before deployment. VicOne Rthena supports threat detection and responses within approved policies during operation.

Figure 2. Cybersecurity strengthens robot safety evidence throughout the lifecycle. VicOne helps teams test safety limits against manipulation before deployment and monitor the conditions behind safe behavior in operation.VicOne

Faster vulnerability discovery matters when teams can turn findings into action: identify what needs attention, verify that safeguards still hold, and confirm that a fix does not introduce new risks. That is how cybersecurity strengthens robot safety as systems continue to change.

For a deeper look how cybersecurity can affect robot safety, download our white paper, “Why Robot Safety Depends on Cybersecurity: Protecting the Information That Safety Decisions Rely On.”

VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety. Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, the company provides automotive and robotics organizations with software and services to identify cyber risks early, assess their potential safety impact, and protect systems in operation, helping maintain safe, reliable behavior across real-world deployments.

The built-in temperature control is customizable to the degree and the steam wand makes gorgeous latte art without breaking a sweat.

Usually $1,599, the Breville Dual Boiler is the ideal "next step" espresso machine with, you guessed it, two boilers powering steam and espresso independently. This model comes with the Breville Smart Grinder Pro, usually $199 — so you're saving $300 overall.

I'm currently testing the Meraki Gen 2, and boy, oh boy, it's a beast. With 45 grinder settings, an almost commercially powerful steam wand, and integrated grinding scale and espresso scale, this is the espresso machine to end all espresso machines. It streamlines every part of the espresso flow. Of course, it's a huge investment, but I love this machine.

#3107. Advanced Metrology for Defect Detection, Tool Health, and Semiconductor Yield Enhancement



In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar shows how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.

In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.

In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also shows how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.

What You Will Learn:

  • How surface scan metrology in station monitors tracks tool health and supports the qualification of thin film deposition processes
  • How baseline signatures and real-time monitoring detect particle generation, hardware degradation, and process drift before production is affected
  • How in-line scans on patterned wafers reveal layer-level defects and show how they propagate through multi-layer device structures
  • When offline 3D optical profilometry should follow in-line inspection, and how it measures dimensions and separates sample defects from foreign material
  • How correlating tool health data, inspection results, and electrical performance links physical defects to yield loss and guides targeted improvement projects

#3105. Saatva customers love the Graphite Pillow and gave it 4.4 stars, so why did I hate it after sleeping on it for a week?

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Unlock and manage exclusive Tom’s Guide member rewards.

Join the Tom's Guide Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow is crafted from a shredded latex core, sandwiched between two memory foam slabs. And that seems to be where the bulk of my issues with this pillow stem from. Despite being graphite infused, the pillow occasionally felt warm and stuffy to me, even during cold nights. Comfort-wise, the bottom of the pillow flattens when you lay your head on it. Depending on which position I slept, I found my neck was either bent in an uncomfortable angle, or my head just slid off. Honestly, it’s hard to know who to suggest this pillow to. Especially when Saatva offers much more comfortable alternatives, like the Cloud Memory Foam Pillow.

Standard loft too shallow for side sleepers but too high for back sleepers

Head slid off pillow when stomach sleeping

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Saatva is renowned for making some of the best mattresses on the market for a luxurious sleep experience. And I should know, I've tested several of them. Which is why I was looking forward to trying out the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow, a pillow the brand recommends to hot sleepers in all sleep positions. Disappointingly, the reality didn't live up to the expectation.

Type: Memory foam and latexBest for: Combination sleepersSizes: standard and high loftTrial: 45 nightsWarranty: 1-yearPrice: $165 at Saatva

As the name suggests, the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow is made with mostly memory foam with a little bit of shredded natural latex thrown into the mix. It has a different design to any of the best pillows I've tested before — a thin shredded latex core, sandwiched by two slabs of graphite-infused memory foam for, apparently, improved breathability (spoiler: this was not my experience).

I tested a queen-size Graphite Memory Foam Pillow in standard loft, but it's also available in a high loft. The surface is on the firmer side and, thanks to its memory foam construction, offers a little contouring. Although I prefer a plusher feel, the surface isn’t what makes this pillow uncomfortable. It was how the bottom edge of the pillow seemed to squish flat, causing my neck to sit at an unnatural angle, or my head to slide off — depending on which position I was sleeping in.

Another big drawback had to do with the temperature regulation. Despite testing during November when my house was cool at night, I woke up to warm spots on the pillow.

If you've read enough and want a quick signpost to a more comfortable alternative, check out my review of the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow (I rated it 4.5/5).But if you're still wondering if the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam pillow could be the right fit for you, strap yourself in for my full review below.

Saatva is a premium mattress brand, and that’s reflected in the price of their pillows too. The Graphite Memory Foam Pillow has an MSRP price of $165 for a standard loft, queen size pillow. Bedding and accessories aren't included in the current Saatva Black Friday sale. However, you do stand to save $40 when you buy as part of a Sateen Sheet Set bundle.

In my opinion, the $165 price tag is steep, especially considering how much of the pillow is comprised of memory foam and there are no certifications for the organic cotton cover or the natural latex.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

A 45-night trial is a bit longer than other brands, however, a 1-year warranty is on the low end for a premium-priced pillow.

The Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow is available in two different lofts and costs $165. While regular Saatva mattress sales shave hundreds off of the best Saatva mattresses during major sale events, pillows and bedding aren't included in those discounts as standalone products. This pillow includes 45 night sleep trial, 1-year warranty and free shipping.

Like many of the best pillows we've tested, there’s a lot more going on with the design of this pillow than appears from the outside. It’s sold in a standard (4-5" tall) or high loft (6-7" tall), with the high loft more suitable to broader bodies.

The pillow effectively has three main layers, starting with a removeable knit cotton cover. Below the cotton cover is an 'inner pillow.' Two medium-thick blocks of memory foam infused with graphite are placed on the front and the back sides of the inner pillow. Memory foam is not a breathable foam, so graphite is used to promote a cool night’s sleep.

Between the memory foam blocks is a bag that contains shredded natural latex and memory foam. It’s quite thin and can be removed entirely from the inner pillow if need be. However, you can’t open that core to add or remove the shredded foams.

Lastly, the memory foam has a CertiPUR-US certification. Although Saatva say the cover is made with organic cotton and they include natural latex in the pillow, no other certifications are provided that verify this.

After one week of testing, here’s what I can tell you about the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow’s comfort and temperature regulation.

The Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow arrived in a plastic bag within a cardboard box. It was already fully expanded, so I was able to take it out of the bag and sleep on it right away. Unfortunately, I noticed off gassing from this pillow right away, and even more so when I slept on the pillow. As someone with a sensitive nose, I tried to sleep on my back, so I wouldn’t have to smell the pillow.

A week before I tested Saatva’s Graphite Memory Foam Pillow, I tested the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow. I’m not a huge fan of memory foam but I found the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow to be extremely comfortable. Unfortunately, I couldn’t say the same of the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow.

I ordered it in the standard loft size which, according to its dimensions, should have been the perfect size to allow me to sleep on my back, stomach, and side. However, it didn’t matter which way I slept, I couldn’t find any position that was particularly comfortable. And there is a single reason why.

When I laid my head down, it didn’t sink into the pillow very much. There was some slight contouring. But at the same time, the bottom length of the pillow (near my shoulders), flattened down creating a significant angle that offered no support to my neck or shoulders. I tried to move the inner shredded latex and memory foam core to prevent this flattening, but nothing seemed to work.

If I slept on my stomach, my head would slide off the pillow. On my side or my back? My neck would feel strained. Because the bottom had flattened out, my neck was not being held up and thus would dip down at an odd angle. If I was lying on my back, my head would be pushed forward more – which wasn’t comfortable. On my side, I was having to hold my head in place or put my hand under the bottom of the pillow to sort of fluff it up.

All in all, I did not sleep well on this pillow during testing.

Bedding brands have long claimed that infusing graphite into memory foam can offer significant cooling properties. I haven’t ever experienced such a thing, not with Saatva’s Graphite Memory Foam Topper and not with this Graphite Memory Foam Pillow.

I didn’t wake up hot and sweaty when sleeping on this pillow. However, I would wake up and notice warm spots around my head. This was odd considering I tested the pillow in November when my home dropped to the 60s at night. I used a breathable Quince linen pillowcase during this time, too.

I think the lack of breathability in this pillow has a lot to do with the design, in particular, those two blocks of memory foam on the front and back of the pillow. Memory foam doesn’t allow for much air to flow through and dissipate heat.

Most pillows should be replaced after two years. However, if you notice the loft breaking down quicker or your pillow having trouble bouncing back if you fold it in half, you should replace it as soon as possible.

I only slept on the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow for one week, and in that time, I haven’t noticed any signs of sagging or breakdown. Saatva include high-quality, premium materials in their products and estimates longer lifespans for their bedding, so I’m sure you don’t have to worry about this pillow breaking down quickly. That said, the one-year warranty is on the low end of warranties for premium pillow brands.

The cotton cover of the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow is removeable and can be thrown in the wash. Machine wash it on cold with a delicate cycle then tumble dry the cover on low or hang it to dry.

Remember, to wash the cover on occasion as it can absorb sweat stains, facial cream, or even saliva. This will help extend the lifespan of your pillow. If you notice that anything has bled through to the inner pillow, you can spot clean it as needed.

Usually when I test a pillow, there’s at least one type of sleeper I can suggest the pillow to – but that’s not the case with the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow. Not only does it sleep warm at night, but the design of the pillow resulted in a variety of issues for my neck or head no matter if I was sleeping on my side, stomach, or back.

The materials aren’t certified organic or completely non-toxic and you can only wash the cover. At least you get the chance to order it in standard or high loft. Considering all the flaws, the price doesn’t feel worth it, even with a 45-night trial with free returns.

I hate to say this about a Saatva product, but they have plenty of others like the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow or the Cloud Memory Foam Pillow that are far more comfortable and/or worth their price.

✅ You're a stomach sleeper with a small build: The pillow flattens considerably along the bottom edge, so it is easier (albeit, not particularly comfortable) to lay your head on the pillow when sleeping on your stomach. Just be mindful that your head might slip off as the pillow doesn’t always provide enough contouring or sink in to prevent such a thing.

✅ You want a pillow with a removeable cover: Thankfully, you can remove the cotton cover of this pillow and easily throw it into the wash.

✅ You want 45 days to try it out: Most pillows come with a 30-day trial, but Saatva allows you to try this pillow for 45 days and will offer a full refund and free return if it’s not to your liking.

❌ You sleep hot: I experienced warm spots when sleeping on this pillow at night – and that’s coming from someone who doesn’t sleep hot. Notably, testing was done in late fall when the evenings were particularly cool in my house.

❌ You like more of a sink in feel to your pillow: While the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow offers a bit of contouring, your head won’t sink in that much. It’s better described as having a firm surface.

❌ You want more neck support: The bottom edge of the pillow flattens which doesn’t offer as much neck support for side sleepers. It also means that when you’re sleeping on your back, it pushes your head forward and creates tension in your neck.

Where the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow has a shredded foam core, the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow’s entire inner filling is comprised of shredded latex and memory foam. This results in a far more comfortable and supportive feel and superb temperature regulation. Best yet? The Cloud Memory Foam is $30 cheaper making it a far better buy.

If you prefer a cleaner or non-toxic night of sleep, consider the Birch Organic Pillow as it is made with shredded latex foams within a layer of wool padding. You’ll experience a cooler night’s sleep on this pillow that starts out with a $149 (originally $198) price tag. However, if you’re a stomach or side sleeper with wide shoulders, it may not be the best option.

The Purple GridCloud Pillow features the brand’s signature Gelflex grid as well as a microfiber fill resulting in a luxury plush feel and a pillow that does not flatten. Despite its lack of size, firmness, or loft options, the Purple GridCloud Pillow has great temperature regulation and is ideal for side and back sleepers. Even the $149 price is more affordable than the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam pillow.

Alex Temblador is a freelance mattress reviewer and writer who has tested a range of traditional and smart mattresses for Tom's Guide. These include the Sleep Number i8 smart bed, the PlushBeds Botanical Bliss luxury organic mattress, and our favorite cooling bed the Bear Elite Hybrid. Alex also reviews bedding and other sleep products for Tom's Guide, including the Brooklinen All-Season Down Comforter and the BeautyRest Black Luxury Foam Pillow. Elsewhere, Alex's work has been published at Dwell, Real Homes, Architectural Digest, and Gardeningetc. When Alex isn’t reviewing sleep and home products, she’s building her career as the award-winning author of two novels, Secrets of the Casa Rosada and Half Outlaw, from her home base in Dallas, Texas.

#3104. Uber lets riders book trips that are filmed from start to finish

The pilot targets late-night trips and rides for teens, using the driver's phone as the camera.

Uber is piloting Recorded Rides in Baltimore, Raleigh, Indianapolis and St. Louis, letting riders book drivers who have turned on video recording for the whole trip. The footage stays encrypted on the driver’s phone and is deleted after 14 days unless it is attached to a safety report.

Uber is testing a ride option in which the whole trip is filmed, TechCrunch reported on Monday. “Recorded Rides” matches riders with drivers who have switched on Uber’s Record My Ride feature, which uses the front camera of the driver’s phone.

The pilot is starting in Baltimore, Raleigh, Indianapolis and St. Louis, with more cities to follow. Uber said it is aimed at late-night trips and rides booked for teens.

Uber is also testing recording that switches on by itself when a car goes off its route, or when the app detects a possible crash. Drivers can opt out in their settings, and riders can decline through an in-app notice, according to TechCrunch. Cameras can protect drivers too: 22 Uber drivers were among more than 50 US gig workers killed on the job over five years, a 2022 study found.

Under Uber’s rules for Record My Ride, the video is encrypted and stored only on the driver’s phone, according to Uber’s help page. Recordings are deleted after 14 days unless they are sent in with a safety report or insurance claim. Uber says it can share them with police under legal process or in an emergency.

Uber first tested recording trip audio in 2019, and has lately added cameras for younger riders. In August, it let parents watch their teen’s ride live on video through the driver’s phone, though other passengers could appear on the stream. Code in its app also hints at rides for children aged 10 to 12.

#3103. Not upgrading to iPhone 18 Pro or Duo? Here’s what’s coming in 2027

iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo have been out for quite some time now, and despite that, it’s still incredibly challenging to order an iPhone Duo in a timely manner. If for whatever reason you’re considering skipping out on this year’s iPhones, here’s what you have to look forward to next year.

2027 is going to be a relatively big iPhone release year for Apple. First, the company will be continuing the iPhone 18 lineup after it introduced a split release schedule. Then, in the fall, the company will debut a new round of flagships in celebration of the 20th anniversary of the iPhone. Here’s what to expect.

For the first time, Apple will be introducing its base iPhone in the spring. Upgrades for the iPhone 18 aren’t quite clear, though more RAM is one of the key rumors. Thermal upgrades will likely happen as well, as well as the new Apple C2 modem.

It’s possible Apple will update the design to fall more in line with the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro, though we don’t yet know.

This phone will of course equip the A20 chip, and it’ll probably start at the same $899 price point that iPhone 17 currently sits at – after it was increased from $799 in September.

This phone will most likely just end up being a chip bump from the A19 to A20 chip, and debut in the Spring alongside the iPhone 18. Earlier this year, reports indicated that Apple would share many components between the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, though it isn’t quite clear what that could mean for the devices.

Out of all of the spring iPhone releases, this one is the one to look forward to. After receiving a lukewarm reception with the initial iPhone Air model, Apple went back to the drawing board and decided to modify the design to fit an ultrawide camera into the device.

Personally, I don’t think an ultrawide camera is too important – though many people will see one camera on the back of the phone and immediately assume it’s less premium, so it’ll probably end up being an important upgrade for the sake of sales. Plus, ultrawide photos can be fun at times.

It should also have a larger battery, reportedly as large as 3500mAh. That’s a roughly 10% improvement from the original iPhone Air. iPhone Air 2 will likely also jump from Apples C1X modem to the C2.

For the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, Apple is expected to debut a fully redesigned iPhone to celebrate. It’ll reportedly be much more glassy, feature significantly slimmer bezels, a quad curved display, and ditch the flat edge design of the iPhone 12 and later.

Personally, I’m slightly skeptical that this’ll truly be a replacement to the “Pro” phone for thermal reasons, but time will tell. iPhone Duo seemingly has strong thermals while not featuring an aluminum unibody, so my concern might not be relevant. It’ll offer two, larger display sizes: 6.4-inch and 7-inch. This largely comes from the bezel reduction.

I wish they prioritized the Telephoto camera more. I need that (whether it be on an Air or a Duo) way more than an Ultrawide.

If you’re holding out for iPhone 18 Pro, this “iPhone 20” is definitely the phone to wait out for.

Lastly, Apple will release a successor to its just-announced iPhone Duo next fall. Of course, you can expect next-generation Apple Silicon with the A21 Pro chip next year, but there aren’t many other substantial changes expected. Apple may bring proper Face ID to the outer display, an improvement from the recently-announced face unlock, but it’s unclear whether this feature will make the engineering cutoff date.
